_comment: Lives under dashboard/, not the repo root, even though it is READ BY BOTH the Python worker (worker/media_limits.py, one directory up) and the dashboard. Turbopack cannot bundle a client-component import from outside its own project root — proven 2026-08-24 by widening turbopack.root, which built successfully but pulled the 1.6GB data/ asset store into the build's file-trace manifest, an unacceptable cost for a tidier file location. A checked-in generated copy was also rejected: two files that must be kept in sync is the exact drift risk this design exists to eliminate. One awkwardly-placed file beats either alternative.

video.note: Meta Page video docs read 2026-08-23: <=1GB, <=20 min via file_url, any aspect ratio. Not yet confirmed by a live publish.
Meta Reels publishing docs read 2026-08-23. Aspect range INCLUSIVE both ends - 16:9 landscape IS permitted. Mirrors worker/publisher.py's _validate. Not yet confirmed by a live publish.

Meta IG User Media reference ('Reel Specifications' section, #reels-specs), read 2026-08-24: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-user/media/ (page shows 'Updated: Aug 12, 2026'). Verbatim: 'Duration: 15 mins maximum, 3 seconds minimum'; 'File size: 300MB maximum'; 'Maximum columns (horizontal pixels): 1920'; 'Required aspect ratio is between 0.01:1 and 10:1 but we recommend 9:16'. Instagram feed video publishes through the Reels container (media_type=REELS shared to feed), so this IS the Reels spec - re-read independently today and it AGREES with dashboard/lib/video-spec.ts's REEL_SPEC (verified 2026-07-28): 300MB, 3s-15min, 1920px max width all match exactly. No discrepancy found. Frame rate (23-60 FPS), codec (MOV/MP4, H264/HEVC, AAC), bitrate (25Mbps video / 128kbps audio) and the moov-atom-at-front requirement are also documented but have no field in this schema - see reference.md for the full text.

image.note: Meta IG User Media reference ('Image Specifications' section), read 2026-08-24: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-user/media/. Verbatim: 'File size: 8 MB maximum'; 'Aspect ratio: Must be within a 4:5 to 1.91:1 range'. Matches reference.md's existing 2026-07-23 note. width is DELIBERATELY OMITTED: the same doc says 'Minimum width: 320 (will be scaled up to the minimum if necessary)' and 'Maximum width: 1440 (will be scaled down to the maximum if necessary)' - Meta auto-scales an out-of-range width rather than refusing it, and this schema has only one severity per field (refuse), so encoding min_width/max_width here would refuse media Meta actually accepts. That is the exact failure mode this task exists to avoid.

video.note: Meta IG User Media reference ('Story Video Specifications' section), read 2026-08-24: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-user/media/. Verbatim: 'Duration: 60 seconds maximum, 3 seconds minimum'; 'File size: 100MB maximum'; 'Maximum columns (horizontal pixels): 1920'; 'Required aspect ratio is between 0.1:1 and 10:1 but we recommend 9:16'. This is the number behind the owner's original bug report: a Story video now has a verified 60s ceiling to check against. Not wired into the composer or worker yet - that is Task 4.

image.note: Meta IG User Media reference ('Story Image Specifications' section), read 2026-08-24: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-user/media/. Verbatim: 'File size: 8 MB maximum'. Aspect ratio DELIBERATELY OMITTED: unlike feed images ('Must be within a 4:5 to 1.91:1 range'), this section only says 'We recommended 9:16 to avoid cropping or blank space' - a recommendation, not a stated range, so there is no verified bound to enforce.

Meta Threads API docs, 'Image Specifications' section, read 2026-08-24: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/threads/posts (page's own metadata reads 'Apr 14, 2026'). Verbatim: 'Format: JPEG and PNG image types are the officially supported formats for image posts.'; 'File Size: 8 MB maximum.'; 'Aspect Ratio Limit: 10:1'. Byte count follows the same binary-MB assumption as Instagram's identical '8 MB maximum' figure (see instagram.feed.image's note) for consistency, not a literal Meta-stated byte count. min_aspect and min_width/max_width DELIBERATELY OMITTED: the page states only a single-sided 'Aspect Ratio Limit: 10:1' (no minimum stated anywhere, unlike Instagram's explicit '4:5 to 1.91:1' range), and separately 'Minimum Width: 320 (will be scaled up to the minimum if necessary)' / 'Maximum Width: 1440 (will be scaled down to the maximum if necessary)' - Meta auto-scales an out-of-range width rather than refusing it, the exact reasoning instagram.feed.image's note already gives for omitting width there. Video Specifications are also on this page (container/codec/duration/1GB/300s) but are NOT recorded anywhere in this file: worker/clients.py's PLATFORM_CAPS['threads'].video_surfaces is empty (frozenset()) - this worker has no Threads video publish path to gate.

image.varies: Discord's own developer docs, read 2026-08-24: https://discord.com/developers/docs/reference#uploading-files. Verbatim: 'The file upload size limit applies to each file in a request. The default limit is 10 MiB for all users, but may be higher for users depending on their Nitro status or by the server's Boost Tier.' Two independent, per-account/per-server factors (the poster's Nitro tier, the destination server's Boost Tier) this install has no way to read at runtime - the only Discord credential here is a webhook URL (worker/clients.py: uses_account_id=False), which carries no user or guild context to query either factor from. No single number is honest here, so max_bytes is left null and this entry exists only to record that the limit is KNOWN to vary, not merely unresearched - a violation from this entry would WARN (per worker/media_limits.py's check(): severity is 'warn' whenever 'varies' is set), though since max_bytes is null no size check ever actually fires; the entry documents the finding rather than enforcing anything.
image.note: https://discord.com/developers/docs/reference#uploading-files, read 2026-08-24. See the 'varies' field above for the full quote and reasoning.

core.telegram.org/bots/api, 'Sending files' section, read directly from the raw page 2026-08-24 (fetched past the AI-summary layer, which was dropping this section). Verbatim: 'Post the file using multipart/form-data in the usual way that files are uploaded via the browser. 10 MB max size for photos, 50 MB for other files.' (The by-URL path, not used here, is smaller: 'Provide Telegram with an HTTP URL for the file to be sent... 5 MB max size for photos and 20 MB max for other types of content.') This worker uploads bytes directly - PLATFORM_CAPS['telegram'].uploads_media_bytes=True in worker/clients.py - so the direct-upload figure applies, not the URL figures. The 10 MB (not 50 MB) direct figure is used because this worker only ever calls sendPhoto/sendMediaGroup (see reference.md's Telegram section) - never sendDocument - so every Telegram asset is a 'photo' in Telegram's own vocabulary, not one of the 'other files' the 50 MB figure covers. Byte count is 10 * 1024 * 1024, the same binary-MB convention as every other entry in this file. A local Bot API server would raise this to 2000 MB, but nothing in this codebase runs one.
